name: Rooster Wake
description:
Rooster Wake lets Claude reach the computers you already own. Ask it to wake a machine that's asleep, check what's up right now, hold a machine awake for exactly as long as you need, or put it back to sleep when you're done — each machine answered by name, from any Claude chat on any device.

The headline act is Remote AI: one request wakes your dev machine, holds it awake, starts Claude Code headlessly in a folder you registered in advance, and hands you the live session in the Claude app. Your machine sleeps until you want it — no desktop left running around the clock, no remote-desktop window on a phone screen just to type one command.

How it works: waking is a Wake-on-LAN broadcast on your own network, sent by an emitter that is awake — the free Rooster Wake agent on any machine that stays on, or our optional dongle. The agent also reports presence honestly (up, asleep as of when, restarting) and carries the power verbs. Sleep always asks you to confirm; there is deliberately no shutdown by voice or chat.

What you need: a free Rooster Wake account, and the agent installed on the PCs you want to reach. Remote AI sessions additionally need Claude Code installed and signed in on the machine (your install, your Anthropic account — we start and stop the process and never see the conversation or your credentials). Waking is free; power actions and unmetered sessions ride the paid plans, and every plan includes three Remote AI sessions a month.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Rooster Wake to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Rooster Wake to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp.roosterwake.com/mcp. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the Rooster Wake MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rooster Wake provides these MCP tools: hold_awake, list_machines, machine_status, prepare_wake, release_awake, sleep_machine, start_claude_session, stop_claude_session, and wake_machine.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Rooster Wake?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 18, 2026, alternatives to Rooster Wake in productivity on the Manufact MCP catalog include Autodesk Product Help, BoardWise, FlagStat, Keenable Web Search, and PomoDial.

_published_faq.name: Does Rooster Wake MCP require authentication?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rooster Wake requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.
Rooster Wake is developed by Puresoft Ltd. It is listed as community on the Claude connector directory.
